objective: Remove M136's redundant second 512-bit response slot and one delivery stage by coupling the fixed-latency macro response directly to the consumer, capturing only on stall.

architecture.fallthrough: correct response directly drives consumer when ready
architecture.stall_action: capture exactly one response and revoke further request credit until released
architecture.maximum_admitted_issue_rate: one accepted read per clock when consumer remains ready

expected_pass_line: PASS M137 fallthrough tagged 16-bank response bridge VCS requests=128 outputs=128 words=2048 ii1=120 stalls=12 skid_buffer=12 row_crossings=120 wrong_token=1 missing=1 unsolicited=1 illegal_base=1 reset_recoveries=4 skid_depth=1 macro_latency=1 delivery_latency=1 macro=false physical_speedup=false system_speedup=false headline=false
paper_safe_statement: Commercial VCS validates a fall-through fixed-one-cycle bridge that preserves M136's 128-request numeric/attack scope, sustains interval-one requests when ready, and uses one 512-bit skid instead of a two-entry return FIFO. Actual DC area delta, SRAM macros, per-bank skew, energy and system speedup remain unadmitted.
prohibited_claims: Do not translate removal of 512 architectural storage bits into measured area or power before matched DC/PTPX.
Do not imply that foundry SRAM macros natively echo transaction tokens.
Do not call one-cycle fall-through a physical or system speedup.
